commit.message:
fix(app,post): refuse a turning op whose fitted axis is not the lathe spindle

The turning kernels fit their axis from the part's facets, while the
lathe post writes X as the diameter about the work offset's origin and
Z as world Z. A part leaning a few degrees in Y with its X on the origin
kept every move in one meridian, passed the post's off-meridian check,
and posted a taper silently.

collect_job now runs operation::spindle_law::check for every turning-
family op and the lathe's axial Drill: the fitted axis line must stand
within 0.0005 mm (radius; half the diameter word's 0.001 mm digit) of
world Z through the op's work-offset origin (posting::wcs_context, the
origin the post receives) at both the part's lowest and highest Z - one
budget for lean and offset. The refusal names the lean in degrees, the
offset in mm, the slot, and says to align the part / move the offset.
Lying axes and non-revolved models pass through to the turning frame's
own refusals. Valid programs post byte-identically (lathe goldens
unchanged); no post-side check was added (see RECOMMENDED.md).

Pinned by lathe_spindle_law:
a_bar_leaning_in_y_on_the_origin_is_refused_by_name_at_generation,
a_plumb_bar_off_the_work_origin_is_refused_by_name_at_generation,
an_axial_drill_on_a_bar_off_the_work_origin_is_refused_by_name,
a_plumb_bar_on_the_origin_or_under_a_moved_work_offset_posts_the_same_program.

Fixes #62

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(app): the lathe spindle law reads the live work offset at the post and bounds the whole part's displacement

Review fixes on PR #65:

- Post-time door: posting::program_ops re-reads the spindle law for
  every turning op and the lathe Drill against the live wcs_context
  origin (before the freshness check), refusing by name - a G54 moved
  after generation no longer posts diameters measured from the old one.
  current_stamp also digests the selected slot's origin for those kinds
  (only off the world origin, so no existing digest moves): the op
  reads Stale too.
- Measure: every part vertex is read about the fitted axis and about
  world Z through the origin; the worst radius or height disagreement
  must be within 0.0005 mm. A lean now counts R*a on faces, so a thin
  wide washer that passed the old axis-at-the-extremes law is refused.
- Fit: multiaxis::axis_refine refines the eigen direction from the
  normal lines' Plucker concurrency rows (4x4 Gauss-Newton), kept only
  past a 1e-12 rad floor and when the fit residual does not grow. An
  uneven f32 24-segment shaft read 1.1 um (a false refusal) before,
  1.4e-7 mm after; worst STL-like noise 3.3e-6 mm. Goldens unchanged.
- Wording: "within one last digit".

Pinned by lathe_spindle_law:
